# A weather app: proving the framework can be pretty

**Status: done.** `bb weather` works, `docs/weather.png` is generated by
`bb shot weather`. Notes on what actually happened are at the bottom.

## Goal

The monitor proved this can look *tidy* -- libadwaita boxed lists, correctly
used. A weather app has to prove it can look **designed**: big type, colour that
means something, a layout that is not just a list of rows.

Second deliverable, same as before: one screenshot, plus an app worth keeping.

## Why weather, specifically

It wins on the numbers, not just on looks.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **No API key** | Open-Meteo needs no signup. Nothing to store, no onboarding screen, anyone can run `bb weather` immediately. |
| **No images** | Beauty comes from typography, colour and stock icons. So memory stays around the monitor's 167 MB instead of the 300-400 MB an image grid would cost. |
| **Fixed layout** | 24 hourly entries, 7 day rows, a handful of detail rows -- always. Rows are created once and patched, which dodges *both* remaining framework gaps: no keyed children needed, and no widget-lifetime problem. |
| **Genuinely daily** | It earns a place on a dock, which a one-off tool does not. |

That last row is the important one. An RSS reader or a wallpaper grid would force
callback-lifetime work first. This does not, so the app can be built without
paying down debt in the same step.

## Phase 0 -- spikes. Done.

All verified before writing this plan:

- **Open-Meteo**, keyless, HTTP 200, ~6 KB per call. One request returns
  `:current`, `:hourly` (168 entries) and `:daily` (7), with `timezone=auto`
  resolving to a real zone and an `:elevation`.
- **Geocoding**, also keyless: `/v1/search?name=Brno` returns name, country,
  admin1, lat, lon. That is the city picker, with no map needed.
- **Icons**: every weather name we need is already in the Adwaita theme,
  including night variants and sunrise/sunset. `wind-symbolic` and
  `temperature-symbolic` are *not* there -- use text labels for those.
- **The look**: a CSS `linear-gradient` on a widget and a 72px light-weight
  label both render correctly. Screenshotted and eyeballed. This is the whole
  beauty mechanism, so it mattered most.
- `clojure.data.xml`, `cheshire` and `babashka.http-client` are built into bb, so
  again: zero dependencies.

## The design

```
AdwWindow
  AdwToolbarView
    AdwHeaderBar            city name as title, search + refresh buttons
    scroll
      hero                  gradient background, chosen by condition
        72px temperature, condition, feels-like, today's high/low
      hourly strip          next 24h, horizontally scrolling
      7-day list            boxed list: icon, day, precipitation %, high/low
      details group         humidity, wind, sunrise, sunset, elevation
```

### The colour engine

This is what makes it look designed rather than assembled. Weather code plus
day/night maps to a gradient: clear day is warm blue, clear night deep indigo,
overcast flat grey-blue, rain steel, storm near-black, snow pale.

**Decision worth recording:** define *every* gradient as a class in one
stylesheet up front (`.sky-clear-day`, `.sky-rain-night`, ...) and switch the
hero's `:class`. The alternative -- rebuilding the stylesheet on each change --
would churn CSS providers on every refresh, and `load-css!` stacks rather than
replaces.

## Phases

### Phase 1 -- the data layer, pure and offline-testable

`examples/openmeteo.clj`: fetch, parse, and a `view-model` that produces exactly
what the UI renders. Same split that worked for `sysinfo`.

The WMO weather code table (0-99) lives here, mapping each code to a label, an
icon name and a sky class, with day and night variants.

**Tests must not need the network.** Capture one real response as a fixture and
test `view-model` against that. A separate, explicitly-run check can hit the
live API; `bb test` stays offline and deterministic.

### Phase 2 -- the look, screenshotted early

Stylesheet plus the hero alone, with hardcoded numbers. Screenshot it. If that
image is not beautiful, the idea is wrong and nothing after this matters. Same
reality check as the monitor's phase 3, and it is the cheapest moment to fail.

### Phase 3 -- the rest of the layout

Hourly strip, 7-day list, details. Needs one small addition: horizontal
scrolling, so `gtk_scrolled_window_set_policy` and a `:scroll` prop for it.
Possibly `:carousel` (AdwCarousel) for the hourly strip instead -- decide when
it is on screen.

### Phase 4 -- refresh, cache, offline, city picker

- A worker refreshes every 15 minutes, same pattern as the monitor: fetch off
  the GTK thread, `reset!` a ratom, let the loop render.
- Cache the last response in `~/.config/bb-weather.edn` so the window opens
  with real content instantly, before the first fetch returns.
- When a fetch fails, keep showing cached data with an `AdwBanner` saying how
  old it is. Never an empty window.
- City picker: an entry, the geocoding API, and a short results list. This is
  the one variable-length list in the app -- a few rows, occasionally, which the
  reconciler already handles.

### Phase 5 -- the deliverable

`docs/weather.png` via the same self-screenshot path, then the README.

## Privacy

**No IP geolocation.** Every "detect my location" service works by logging the
caller's address. The city goes in the config file, and the geocoding request
sends only the name you type.

## Done means

- [x] `bb weather` opens something that looks designed, not assembled
- [x] it works offline, showing cached data with an honest staleness banner
- [x] core barely changed: two common props and an entry placeholder
- [x] `bb test` still passes with no network -- both weather test files run from
      a captured fixture
- [x] `docs/weather.png` next to `docs/monitor.png`

## What actually happened

Everything in the plan held. Four things worth recording:

- **It idles at 0.00% of a core**, 223 MB (170 MB while it still forced the
  cairo renderer, which was later dropped everywhere -- see the deck plan). Refreshing every 15 minutes rather
  than every second means the blocking main loop really does nothing in between.
  The monitor's 1.5% is entirely its own once-a-second work.
- **The dashboard collapsed to a 58px sliver** on first run. A `GtkBox` child
  takes its natural height unless told to expand, and a scrolled window's
  natural height is tiny. `:vexpand true` on the main scroll fixed it. Worth
  remembering: the tree was correct, only the allocation was wrong, so nothing
  errored -- it just looked broken.
- **Layout drove two content decisions**, both improvements. "Feels like" was a
  details row duplicating the hero line, and sunrise/sunset were two rows that
  are always read together. Cutting one and merging the other made the app fit a
  screen *and* read better.
- **Six small additions**, none structural: `:halign`/`:valign` as common props,
  a `:placeholder` on `:entry`, scrollbar policy on `:scroll`, and three Adw
  tags (`:clamp`, `:banner`, `:spinner`).

## Deliberately not doing

Radar maps (tiles mean images, network cache and a lot of memory), severe
weather alerts (region-specific feeds), multiple saved cities with swipe
navigation (a variable list of pages, which is where keyed children would start
to bite), and any unit system beyond a metric/imperial toggle.
